* Project Title  
- Equipment API

---

* Installation Setup

	**Step 1: Clone the Repository**

- https\://github.com/Janjann12/MidtermActEquipment-api.git  
- cd MidtermActEquipment-api


	**Step 2: Install Dependencies**	

	Install the required PHP packages.

- Composer install


	**Step 3: Configure the Environment**

	Create a local .env file from existing example configuration in window   powershell:

- Copy-Item .env.example .env


	Generate the Laravel application key:

- Php artisan key:generate

	**Step 4: Configure the SQLite Database**  
	  
	Make sure the SQLite database does not exist. Run this in PowerShell if it does not exist:

- New-Item database/database.sqlite \-ItemType File


	Configure the database connection in the .env file:

- DB\_CONNECTION=sqlite


	**Step 5: Run Migrations**  
	  
	Create the database tables required:

- php artisan migrate


	**Step 6: Start API**

	Start the Laravel Server, keep the server open while you test the APIs  
	The API will be available at [http\://127.0.0.1:8000](http://127.0.0.1:8000):

- Php artisan serve

---

* API Routes

| VERB | PATH | DESCRIPTION | TOKEN  |
| :---: | ----- | ----- | :---: |
| POST | /api/register | Registers a new account | NO |
| POST | /api/login | Authenticate user and returns an API token |  NO |
| GET | /api/logout | Log outs the user and revoke the token | YES |
| POST | /api/me | Retrieve the currently authenticated user’s information | YES |
| GET | /api/equipment | Retrieve all equipment, supports filter by category and quantity | YES |
| POST | /api/equipment | Creates a new equipment record | YES |
| GET | /api/equipment/{id} | Retrieve a record by ID | YES |
| PUT | /api/equipment/{id} | Update a record by ID | YES |
| DELETE | /api/equipment/{id} | Delete a record by ID | YES |

* Why Deleting a Record Returns 204 and not 200  
    
- The DELETE request results in a 204 No Content status because the equipment record has been successfully deleted, and no data to return in the response body. A 200 OK status is generally used when the server provides a response body to confirm the action taken. The 204 status is more suitable when the deletion is successful and no further information needs to be conveyed. This approach enables the API to distinctly communicate success while bypassing the need for an extraneous response body.
